title: When there's no water
hook: a clean earth or dust wipe of face and hands replaces washing (5:6)

segments.voice: Yesterday, ghusl, the full bath, and your line: the whole body clean. Did you take a shower in order, as a beginning? Wudu and ghusl both need water. So what if there isn't any? Day one thousand seventy-seven.

A necklace goes missing in the desert. Aishah has lost it on a journey, and the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, stops the whole caravan so people can look for it. But the place they've stopped has no water, and they're carrying none. The prayer time comes. People go to Aishah's father, Abu Bakr, and complain: look what she's done. Abu Bakr comes and scolds her, while the Prophet ﷺ sleeps with his head on her lap. Then a verse comes down. And when they finally move the camel she'd been riding, there's the necklace, lying underneath it. Sahih al-Bukhari tells it, at number 334. The verse that came is today's word.
screen: `A NECKLACE LOST IN THE DESERT.` → `NO WATER, AND THE PRAYER TIME COMES.` → `A VERSE, AND THE NECKLACE UNDER THE CAMEL.`

segments.voice: The word is tayammum. The verse is the end of 5:6, the same verse that gave wudu and ghusl. It says that if you are sick, or on a journey, or have come from relieving yourself or been intimate, and you find no water, then go to clean earth and wipe your faces and your hands with it. And then, in Pickthall's translation: "Allah would not place a burden on you, but He would purify you." That line is the whole spirit of the ruling. The water ran out, and the prayer didn't. In the story, a companion named Usayd ibn Hudayr said this wasn't the first blessing to come through Abu Bakr's family. A lost necklace became an easing for everyone after. How is it done? Another hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, number 338, has a companion, Ammar ibn Yasir, who needed a full bath on a journey with no water. He didn't know about tayammum yet, so he rolled in the dust like an animal, and prayed. When he told the Prophet ﷺ, he was shown something much simpler: strike the earth with your hands, blow on them, wipe your face and your hands. That's it. The schools differ on the details, one strike or two, the hands to the wrist or further, but the shape is the same, and it stands in for wudu and for ghusl alike. Another hadith, Bukhari 335, gives the Prophet ﷺ saying the earth has been made for him a place of prayer and a means of purification. Water, when there is water. Clean earth, when there isn't.
screen: `NO WATER: GO TO CLEAN EARTH.` · `NOT A BURDEN, BUT A PURIFYING.` · `AMMAR ROLLED IN THE DUST.` · `STRIKE, BLOW, WIPE FACE AND HANDS.` · then, large: `ALLAH WOULD NOT PLACE A BURDEN ON YOU.`

segments.voice: The practice: learn the motions. Settle, and rest your palms flat on whatever is beneath you, a table, the floor, your knees. Feel how ordinary that surface is. Now, slowly, lift your hands, and in your mind wipe your face with them, once. Then wipe the back of one hand with the other, and switch. That's the shape of tayammum. If you pray, you'll know these motions the day you need them. If you don't, sit with the idea in it: when the usual way is closed, there's still a way. The bell holds the time.
Tayammum. The dry purification: clean earth, the face and the hands, in place of water when there's none or it would harm you. Today's word.
Your line: the earth is clean. Today, when something you usually rely on isn't there, look for the way that's still open. Tomorrow, the adhan's words. Day one thousand seventy-seven.

howItsDone: When Muslims have no water, or water would harm them through illness, they make tayammum: they strike clean earth or dust with their hands and wipe the face and hands, then pray; it stands in for both wudu and ghusl until water is available.

original.note: Arabic: the dry purification with clean earth.

trapdoor: what you thought: no water means no prayer.
what it means: clean earth on the face and hands stands in for washing, for wudu and for ghusl.
what a scholar hears: the end of 5:6, the necklace of Bukhari 334, and Ammar's lesson in Bukhari 338, with the schools differing on strikes and how far the hands are wiped.

sources.quoted: Allah would not place a burden on you, but He would purify you

notes: Pickthall 5:6 ('Allah would not place a burden on you, but He would purify you') quoted from memory; confirm. The rest of 5:6 is paraphrased.

Bukhari 334 (Aishah's necklace, Abu Bakr's rebuke, the Prophet asleep on her lap, Usayd ibn Hudayr's remark, the necklace under the camel), Bukhari 335 (the earth made a place of prayer and purification) and Bukhari 338 (Ammar rolling in the dust; strike, blow, wipe face and hands) numbers and details to confirm. Some narrations of 334 connect it to 4:43 rather than 5:6; Keeper to decide which verse to name.
School differences (one strike or two; hands to the wrists or to the elbows) stated generally; confirm. Ja'fari practice wipes the forehead and backs of the hands; Keeper may add.
'Or it would harm you' in the word segment reflects the verse's mention of sickness; confirm the phrasing.
Editor: fork reworded to ask what Ammar did, so rolling in the dust isn't presented as the right choice; carry names tomorrow.
